title: Addict crashes car, shoots up one last time: Victoria man dies in police custody
article: After travelling the wrong way on the Trans-Canada Highway and crashing into a concrete barrier, a 45-year-old Victoria man struggling to beat a cocaine addiction shot up one last time in his car before dying.
Within the hour, David Kenneth Smelts was pronounced dead in hospital at 8:26 p.m. Friday.
Because he was in police custody at the time, Smelts's death is being investigated by the Island District Major Crime Unit and B.C. Coroner Service.
It will also be the subject of a public inquest.

RCMP Cpl. Gord Bedingfield said a police officer arrived at the crash scene just after 7:30 p.m., and she immediately called for backup because Smelts motioned in a threatening fashion at her with the needle he was using.
Smelts was subdued, shoved down on the ground and handcuffed, Bedingfield explained.
But some time later Smelts began exhibiting signs he was in "medical distress" and was taken to hospital by ambulance.
According to coroner Barb McLintock he "did not have a pulse at that time" upon arrival at the hospital at 8:07 p.m.
Doctors worked to resuscitate him and he was pronounced dead almost 20 minutes later. A full autopsy will be conducted later this week.
The coroner will determine whether internal injuries from the crash, drugs use, or a medical condition resulting from drug use caused his death.
The public inquest, which will likely occur in the spring, will determine if anything could have been done differently to prevent Smelts's death.
